data.current_description: Creates the business and claims its permanent public @handle. It SPENDS NOTHING: describing a business comes before paying for one, so an account with no plan may call this, and the paid setup — the content workspace, the app backend, the subdomains — is released later by the payment projection. An account that already pays gets that release before the response. Answers 201 for a new row and 200 when a double-submit resolved to a row that already existed.
data.description_suggestion: Creates a new business workspace and claims its permanent public @handle. The operation requires a NewBusiness object with the business details and desired handle. No payment is required to create a business; the paid infrastructure (workspace, app backend, subdomains) is provisioned based on the account's subscription status. Accounts without a plan can create businesses; paid setup is deferred until payment. Returns 201 if a new business was created, or 200 if the request was a duplicate of an existing business (idempotent). The response includes the created or existing Business object.

data.current_summary: Mint a one-time code for crossing to the product

It is single-use, expires in minutes, is stored only as a hash, and is spent by the product's own /auth/enter page. Never cached.
data.summary_suggestion: Generate a one-time handoff code for product access
data.description_suggestion: Generates a single-use, time-limited handoff code that allows the authenticated user to transition from result.dev to app.result.dev while maintaining their session. The refresh token cannot be shared across hosts due to security restrictions, so this operation provides a temporary code instead. The code expires within minutes, is stored only as a hash on the server, and is consumed by the product's /auth/enter endpoint. Results are never cached. Use this operation when redirecting users from the marketing site to the product workspace.
